description:
FILED s473t3 (Opus triage of the 79 CATALOG-only blessed rows), on main
d9a2aac0.  PRE-EXISTING.  Probe: scratch/s473t3/probes/p06-sprintf2.pl.

ROWS BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, 4 rows):
  sprintf2.t 1509 `subnormal 3e-322 %a 0x1.e8p-1069 got 0x1.ep-1069`
  sprintf2.t 1513 `subnormal 7e-321 %a 0x1.624p-1064 got 0x1.62p-1064`
  sprintf2.t 1514 `subnormal 7e-322 %a 0x1.1cp-1067 got 0x1.1ap-1067`
  sprintf2.t 1519 `subnormal 3e-322 %.4a 0x1.e800p-1069 got 0x1.e000p-1069`

MEASURED (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    printf("%a|%a|%a|%.4a\n", 3e-322, 7e-321, 7e-322, 3e-322)
  perl: 0x1.e8p-1069|0x1.624p-1064|0x1.1cp-1067|0x1.e800p-1069
  PCL : 0x1.ep-1069 |0x1.62p-1064 |0x1.1ap-1067|0x1.e000p-1069
CONTROL: `%a` of 1.5 is `0x1.8p+0` in BOTH -- normal doubles are right.

MECHANISM: the `%a` arm builds its hex digits from `integer-decode-float`,
whose significand for a DENORMAL is not the 53-bit normalized one; the low
bits are dropped (1514 shows an actual wrong digit, `1a` for `1c`, not just a
truncation).  Fix area: the `(#\a)` arm of `sprintf-one` in
`cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` -- renormalize a denormal before extracting digits.

CATALOG NOTE THIS REPLACES: sweep-bug-catalog.md sprintf2.t,
"subnormal/denormal `%a` last-hexdigit rounding (~17t)".  The note calls it
rounding; measured, the SIGNIFICAND is wrong, which is a different fault from
#1477.

FAMILY: float formatting; siblings #1475, #1477.
subject: BUG (sprintf `%a`): the significand of a SUBNORMAL double loses its low hex digits -- `sprintf "%a", 3e-322` is `0x1.e8p-1069` in perl and `0x1.ep-1069` in PCL, and `%.4a` pads with zeros instead of the real bits
